chunks: And from him, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who is performing salat and does not know whether he has prayed one rakʿah or two.
He said: “He starts over until he becomes certain that he has completed [the prayer], and this is in the Friday prayer, in the Maghrib prayer, and in the salat during travel.”

key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel, i.e. the state of journey in which shortened prayer applies
key_terms.يَسْتَقْبِلُ: starts the prayer again from the beginning

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he doubts whether he prayed one or two rakʿahs in Jumuʿah, Maghrib, or travel prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one who doubts the number of rakʿahs prayed in certain prayers. It states that in Jumuʿah, Maghrib, and prayers performed during travel, the person must restart the prayer until certainty of completion is attained.
